review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–93). I also grepped the NavierStokesAndEuler directory for uses of `asymmetricTransport_apply`, `asymmetricTransport_eq` and `asymmetricTransport_eq_background`.

- The file has no `@[simp]` attributes. Its only simp calls are `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, in `asymmetricTransport_apply` and the final step of `asymmetricTransport_bound`.
- `asymmetricTransport_apply` unfolds the map into a sum of `productHq` terms. It is the one candidate for a simp lemma. Downstream code applies it deliberately as `simp only [asymmetricTransport_apply, map_sum]` in SobolevNonlinearCompatibility.lean and as `rw` in this file. Making it a default simp lemma would expand every application into a sum and could interfere with `asymmetricTransport_eq` and `asymmetricTransport_eq_background`, which want the map kept folded. I found no use that would improve, so I did not propose the attribute.
- `asymmetricTransport_eq` and `asymmetricTransport_eq_background` relate this map to `transportBilinear` and `backgroundDrift`. Tagging either as simp would pick one normal form for each pair of equivalent expressions without any evidence from the downstream uses. I saw no cycle or competing rule.
- The two local instances are not simp-relevant.
- I could not run Lean. I did not open the definitions of `productHqBilinear_apply` or `sum_apply`; my grep for simp attributes in SobolevTransport.lean found none.
